transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

My thoughts won’t slow down—they’re racing all the time and I can’t turn them off long enough to focus or rest. It's just gotten to the point where I feel like I can't keep up with my own mind anymore.

Have there been times when you felt unusually high, energized, or irritable for several days with much less need for sleep than usual? Or have these racing thoughts and trouble focusing been more constant over many years?

Yes, I get these intense, amped-up periods where I feel invincible and highly energized, sleeping only about three hours a night but waking up totally wired—though I also get really irritable and snap at my roommate. This isn't a long-term thing from over the years; it actually started about a year ago when I transitioned to full-time freelance work, and it's been happening on and off since then.

Have you ever had a separate period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest in things most of the day, nearly every day? This would help me know whether these high-energy episodes are part of bipolar disorder or a single manic episode.

No, I haven't really experienced periods of feeling deeply depressed or losing interest in things for two weeks or more. My main struggles have really just been the racing thoughts, the high energy, and some of the other strange experiences I've been going through.
Before these high-energy episodes started a year ago, had you ever had any similar episodes earlier in life? Also, have you ever been diagnosed with bipolar disorder or had treatment for it before?
No, I've never experienced anything like these high-energy episodes earlier in my life before this past year. I've also never been diagnosed with or treated for bipolar disorder in the past.

Since these episodes started a year ago, have you had more than one distinct period of this elevated or irritable, high-energy state, with times in between when you were back to your usual self? About how long did each episode last?

Yes, I've had several of these amped-up stretches on and off over the past year. In fact, these high-energy periods dominate most of my time, and I only get short, temporary breaks where I feel closer to my old baseline or a bit flatter, like a quieter spell I had a couple of months ago.

During those quieter periods between the high-energy episodes, have you ever had even one separate episode where you felt depressed or lost interest in most things for at least two weeks? This includes feeling down, empty, hopeless, or unable to enjoy things most of the day nearly every day.

No, I haven't really experienced prolonged periods of feeling deeply depressed, down, or hopeless for two weeks like that. During my quieter spells, my mood just feels a bit flatter or closer to my normal baseline, but it's never been a deep depression.

To tell whether this is bipolar I disorder or a single manic episode, before this past year have you ever had any earlier episodes of the same kind of elevated or irritable mood with very high energy and little need for sleep? Even if they were never diagnosed, did anything like this ever happen before?
No, I haven't experienced anything like this prior to this past year. All of these difficulties only began after I transitioned to full-time freelance work about a year ago.

During these high-energy periods, have you ever had to be hospitalized, gotten into serious trouble at work or with money, or had experiences like hearing voices or believing things others said weren’t true? This helps me tell whether these episodes meet full mania rather than a milder form.

I haven't been hospitalized, but I've faced serious professional setbacks like missing deadlines, losing a major exhibit opportunity, and straining my relationships with collaborators. Also, during my most wired periods, especially this past spring, I heard a male voice commenting on my art and was convinced big galleries were tracking and sabotaging me. It's even made it hard to keep up with basic chores like laundry and meals.

opening_question.question: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has had recurrent distinct episodes over the past year of elevated/irritable mood with markedly increased energy, decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts, and significant impairment, along with psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and persecutory/grandiose beliefs) occurring during the high-energy states. There is no history of major depressive episodes, but bipolar I disorder is still diagnosed when recurrent manic episodes occur; the current/most severe presentation is mania with psychotic symptoms.
